resources.string: Installed outside a store

The app was installed from a file (file manager, package installer, ADB) and not from a store (Play, Galaxy Store, F-Droid). Almost all malware comes this way, but you may have installed a legitimate app yourself.
Installed by another app
The app was installed by an app that is not a known store (browser, messenger, another app). This is the route of software that drops other software; some alternative installers are legitimate.
No icon in the app list
The app has no active launcher icon: it does not appear in the app drawer. Typical of spyware; technical components have none either.
Can send SMS
The app is allowed to send SMS (possibly premium-rate or phishing ones) without your messaging app keeping a trace.
Can read or intercept SMS
The app can read or receive SMS, and therefore steal one-time validation codes.
Access to calls
The app can place calls, answer them or read the call log.
Accessibility service
The app declares an accessibility service: once enabled, it can read the screen, tap on your behalf and type text. This is the power most abused by banking trojans.
Reads notifications
The app declares a notification listener: once enabled, it reads all notifications (messages, one-time codes).
Device administrator
The app declares an administration receiver: it can prevent its own uninstallation, lock or erase the device.
Draws over other apps
The app asks to be displayed on top of other apps: the technique of fake login screens that steal passwords and codes.
Can install other apps
The app asks to install packages: the route of software that downloads then installs its payload. Alternative stores and file managers legitimately ask for it.
VPN service
The app declares a VPN service: once enabled, it can see and redirect all the phone\'s network traffic.
Starts with the device
The app relaunches itself at every phone boot.
Background location
The app can track your location even when you are not using it.
Microphone or camera in the background
The app has access to the microphone or the camera and can run as a microphone or camera foreground service, and therefore record without the screen being devoted to it. Video call apps do the same.
Built for an old Android version
The app targets an Android version older than 11 and escapes several recent protections (storage access, background launch…). Malware does it on purpose; abandoned apps do too.
Debug app
The app is marked "debuggable": code can be injected into it. Unusual outside development.
Banking trojan profile
Combination of accessibility service + overlay + reading of SMS or notifications: everything needed to steal banking credentials and approve transfers without your knowledge.
SMS fraud profile
Combination of sending SMS + starting with the device, for an app that is not your default SMS app: the profile of a mass SMS send in the background.
Stalkerware profile
Combination of no icon + location or microphone + starting with the device: the profile of hidden surveillance software.
Risk profile of apps

Scores each app from 0 to 100 (low, medium, high) from what the system says about it: install source, permissions granted, declared accessibility, notification listener, VPN and administration services, starting with the device, absence of an icon, targeted Android version, debug mode. System apps and Watchpost are capped at "low". Emitted on every install and update, then every day only if the score or its reasons changed (about a hundred events on the first pass). One package walk per day. No app content is read.
Default apps (changes)

Every change of SMS app, dialer, browser, home, assistant, keyboard or autofill app, with the old and the new app. Only what the system lets a third-party app read is tracked (Android does not give the list of role holders to an app, even a Device Owner): call screening, notes, wallet and call forwarding are not visible. The current state stays in "Special access". A few system calls, checked after a change and at most every 15 minutes when the screen turns off.
Sensitive operations usage (experimental)

Every hour: how many times each app sent or read SMS, placed calls, read contacts or the call log, recorded sound, used the camera, read the precise location or the list of accounts, including the share in the background. Read from the system operations history ("dumpsys appops"), whose format is not guaranteed and has never been observed on a physical device. Disabled by default; requires the DUMP and PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS permissions granted through ADB. The first reading is only a reference. Ten readings per hour, bounded in time and size, 300 lines at most. If the format is not recognized, the collector declares itself unavailable with the reason instead of insisting.
DUMP permission not granted: scripts/grant-adb-permissions.sh (or adb shell pm grant io.github.erwsim.watchpost android.permission.DUMP)
PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS permission not granted (the operations service requires it in addition to DUMP): scripts/grant-adb-permissions.sh
The system refuses to read the operations state: DUMP and PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS must be granted through ADB (scripts/grant-adb-permissions.sh).
This Android version does not recognize the "dumpsys appops" options used: unknown format.
"dumpsys appops" returned nothing (reading refused by SELinux or service absent).
The output does not contain the operations history (disabled, or stored elsewhere on this Android version): no counter is available.
The operations history is disabled by the system.
The format of the "dumpsys appops" output is not recognized (unknown Android or One UI version).
The "dumpsys appops" output exceeds the allowed size: reading abandoned.
"dumpsys appops" did not answer in time.
The system refused or could not run the reading (Debug.dumpService failed: SELinux?).
Camera/microphone attribution impossible: DUMP permission not granted (scripts/grant-adb-permissions.sh).
Camera/microphone attribution impossible: PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS permission not granted (the operations service requires it in addition to DUMP; scripts/grant-adb-permissions.sh).
Camera/microphone attribution impossible: the system refuses to read the operations state despite the permissions (DUMP and PACKAGE_USAGE_STATS).
